name: Certificate Parser
description: Parse an X.509 certificate: subject, issuer, validity, extensions, public key and fingerprints.

examples.label: Parse a leaf certificate's subject, extensions and fingerprints

hints.fingerprints: Several algorithms can be computed at once; md5 and sha1 are weak and only useful for legacy interop.
hints.atTime: Leave empty to evaluate against the current time; supply an RFC3339 instant to review historical state.
hints.safe: Read-only: the certificate is never modified and never written to disk.

faq.q: How do I tell whether a certificate is self-signed?
faq.a: The "Self-signed" field is true and the issuer matches the subject.

faq.q: What if the certificate is not valid yet?
faq.a: Validity reports "not yet valid"; fill in the evaluation time to check another instant.

faq.q: Can I use fingerprints to compare certificates?
faq.a: Yes. Each algorithm yields a stable value for a given certificate, and distinct certificates practically never collide.
